# Statement of Reproducibility {.unnumbered}

All code developed for data processing, model training, evaluation, and the operational prototype is fully available in the project's [GitHub repository](https://github.com/klaveflo/satellite-mowing-detection). The ground truth data provided by Zurich Airport is confidential and cannot be publicly shared, but the code structure allows reproduction of the workflow using similar datasets. Sentinel-2 imagery is openly available through the [Copernicus Browser](https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/). Sentinel-1 GRD data were accessed via Google Earth Engine, and SLC products were acquired from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem using the `cdsetool` library. Both sources are publicly accessible, though SLC acquisition requires user credentials that are not included in the repository. The [official land survey and fire brigade responsibility area data](https://geo.zh.ch/) are openly available from the Canton of Zurich geoportal.

To ensure reproducibility and maintainability, set random seeds were used throughout all model training and splitting procedures. The codebase was organised into documented, modular functions in a dedicated `src` directory, preventing code duplication and allowing individual pipeline steps to be reused independently. Key configuration variables and parameters (e.g., temporal window sizes, cloud probability thresholds, feature sets, postprocessing parameters) are declared at the top of each notebook to facilitate adaptation. The standalone prototype notebook for operational mowing detection is fully self-contained and does not depend on the project's source modules. Project version control was managed via GitHub. All computational tasks, including SAR coherence processing via SNAP GPT, were run on standard local hardware.
